currentGoalDescription:
Evolve the Java 21 application into a COMMAND-LINE tool that validates and summarises delimited
  text files. It is not a service: it has no network surface, no HTTP, and no long-running process.
  It reads argv, reads files from disk, writes to stdout and stderr, and terminates with an exit
  status.

  Invocation: java -jar app.jar <command> [arguments]

  Commands:

  check <file> — read the file and report malformed rows. A row is malformed when its field count
  differs from the header's. Print one line per malformed row to stdout as
  "line <n>: expected <h> fields, found <f>", in ascending line order. Exit 0 when every row is
  well formed, exit 2 when at least one row is malformed.

  count <file> — print the number of data rows (excluding the header) to stdout as a bare integer.
  Exit 0.

  column <file> <name> — print every value of the named column, one per line, in file order.
  Exit 0. Exit 4 when the named column is not present in the header, printing
  "no such column: <name>" to stderr.

  Common rules: exit 1 when the file argument names a path that does not exist, printing
  "no such file: <path>" to stderr. Exit 3 when the command word is not one of the three above,
  printing "unknown command: <word>" to stderr. Exit 5 when the wrong number of arguments is given
  for a known command. The first line of a file is always its header. Fields are separated by
  commas. No quoting or escaping is required.

acceptanceCriteria: When invoked with an unknown command (e.g., `java -jar app.jar foo`), the tool prints `unknown command: foo` to stderr and exits with code 3.
When invoked with a known command but incorrect number of arguments (e.g., `java -jar app.jar check`), the tool exits with code 5.
When invoked with a file path that does not exist (e.g., `java -jar app.jar check /nonexistent`), the tool prints `no such file: /nonexistent` to stderr and exits with code 1.
When invoked with `check <file>` where the file exists and all rows are well-formed, the tool exits with code 0 and prints nothing to stdout.

When invoked with `check <file>` where the file exists and contains malformed rows, the tool prints one line per malformed row to stdout in the format `line <n>: expected <h> fields, found <f>` and exits with code 2.
When invoked with `count <file>` where the file exists, the tool prints the number of data rows (excluding header) as a bare integer to stdout and exits with code 0.
When invoked with `column <file> <name>` where the column exists, the tool prints every value of that column one per line to stdout in file order and exits with code 0.
When invoked with `column <file> <name>` where the column does not exist in the header, the tool prints `no such column: <name>` to stderr and exits with code 4.

Implement the `check` command to read a delimited file, validate row field counts against the header, and report malformed rows to stdout with the format "line <n>: expected <h> fields, found <f>", exiting with code 0 if all rows are valid or code 2 if any are malformed.
Implement the `count` command to read a delimited file and print the number of data rows (excluding the header) as a bare integer to stdout, exiting with code 0.

Implement the `column` command to read a delimited file and print every value of the named column, one per line, in file order to stdout, exiting with code 0, or exit with code 4 and print "no such column: <name>" to stderr if the column is not present in the header.
Implement argument count validation for all commands so that when the wrong number of arguments is given for a known command, the application prints an error message to stderr and exits with code 5.

When the application is invoked with a valid command word (e.g., `java -jar app.jar check`), it does not exit with status code 3 due to an unknown command error.
Implement the `check` command to read a: When the `check` command is invoked with a valid file where all rows have the same field count as the header, it exits with status code 0 and prints nothing to stdout.

When the `check` command is invoked with a file containing a malformed row, it prints a line to stdout in the format "line <n>: expected <h> fields, found <f>" for each malformed row in ascending line order, and exits with status code 2.
When the `check` command is invoked with a non-existent file path, it prints "no such file: <path>" to stderr and exits with status code 1.
Implement the `count` command to read a: When the `count` command is invoked with a valid file, it prints the number of data rows (excluding the header) as a bare integer to stdout and exits with status code 0.
When the `count` command is invoked with a non-existent file path, it prints "no such file: <path>" to stderr and exits with status code 1.
Implement the `column` command to read a: When the `column` command is invoked with a valid file and a column name present in the header, it prints every value of that column, one per line, in file order to stdout and exits with status code 0.
When the `column` command is invoked with a valid file and a column name not present in the header, it prints "no such column: <name>" to stderr and exits with status code 4.
When the `column` command is invoked with a non-existent file path, it prints "no such file: <path>" to stderr and exits with status code 1.
Implement argument count validation for: When the `check` command is invoked without a file argument, it exits with status code 5.
When the `count` command is invoked without a file argument, it exits with status code 5.
When the `column` command is invoked without a file argument or without a column name, it exits with status code 5.
